An FC-FC scatter plot (also called a variant volcano plot) compares the fold changes of the same features between two differential contrasts: each point is one gene (or protein, metabolite, …), the X-axis is its log2 fold change in contrast A and the Y-axis its log2 fold change in contrast B. Unlike a volcano plot, which displays one contrast against significance, the FC-FC scatter puts two contrasts side by side, making it easy to identify features that are *consistently* changed in both contrasts (both axes share the same sign), *contrast-specific* (changed on only one axis), or *discordant* (opposite directions) — the typical questions when comparing two datasets, two cell populations, two treatment arms, or discovery and validation cohorts. This tutorial reproduces the chart type covered by the *顶刊图社* series (issue 018); see the Reference section below.

## Example

![](../images/Omics/FcFcPlot_demo.png){fig-alt="FcFcPlot DEMO" fig-align="center" width="70%"}

This FC-FC scatter plot compares the marker-gene statistics of two monocyte subsets: the X-axis is the average log2 fold change of each gene in the CD14+ Mono cluster (versus all remaining cells) and the Y-axis is its average log2 fold change in the FCGR3A+ Mono cluster. Points are colored by significance category: shared markers significant in both subsets (red), subset-specific markers (blue/green) and discordant markers with opposite directions (purple); point size encodes the statistical significance. Classical monocyte markers such as `S100A8`/`S100A9` sit at the extreme right on the CD14+ axis (`S100A9` is even flagged *discordant* because its FCGR3A+ fold change is significantly negative), `MS4A7` deviates upward (FCGR3A+ Mono specific), while a large group along the diagonal (`LST1`, `FCER1G`, `AIF1`, `CD68`, …) are shared monocyte markers.

## Setup

-   System Requirements: Cross-platform (Linux/MacOS/Windows)

-   Programming Language: R

-   Dependencies: `scRNAtoolVis`; `tidyverse`; `ggrepel`

```{r packages setup, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, output=FALSE}
# Installing necessary packages
if (!requireNamespace("scRNAtoolVis", quietly = TRUE)) {
  remotes::install_github("junjunlab/scRNAtoolVis")
}
if (!requireNamespace("tidyverse", quietly = TRUE)) {
  install.packages("tidyverse")
}
if (!requireNamespace("ggrepel", quietly = TRUE)) {
  install.packages("ggrepel")
}

# Load packages
library(scRNAtoolVis)
library(tidyverse)
library(ggrepel)
```

## Data Preparation

The example uses `pbmc.markers`, the PBMC single-cell marker-gene table shipped with the [scRNAtoolVis](https://github.com/junjunlab/scRNAtoolVis) package (9 clusters, 5,921 rows of marker statistics). Each row reports one gene's differential expression statistics in one cluster versus all remaining cells (`avg_log2FC`, `p_val_adj`, `pct.1`, `pct.2`, …). We compare the two monocyte subsets — CD14+ Mono and FCGR3A+ Mono — by joining their marker statistics gene by gene, which gives two "contrasts" of the same feature set.

```{r load data, message=FALSE}
# Load the PBMC marker gene table
data("pbmc.markers")

# Marker statistics of the two monocyte subsets
cd14 <- pbmc.markers |>
  filter(cluster == "CD14+ Mono") |>
  select(gene, avg_log2FC, p_val_adj)

fcgr3a <- pbmc.markers |>
  filter(cluster == "FCGR3A+ Mono") |>
  select(gene, avg_log2FC, p_val_adj)

# Join by gene: 546 genes are markers in both subsets
fc_fc <- inner_join(cd14, fcgr3a, by = "gene", suffix = c("_cd14", "_fcgr3a"))

# Classify each gene and compute the plotting score
fc_cut <- 0.5
p_cut <- 0.05
fc_fc <- fc_fc |>
  mutate(
    sig_cd14 = p_val_adj_cd14 < p_cut & abs(avg_log2FC_cd14) >= fc_cut,
    sig_fcgr3a = p_val_adj_fcgr3a < p_cut & abs(avg_log2FC_fcgr3a) >= fc_cut,
    category = case_when(
      sig_cd14 & sig_fcgr3a & sign(avg_log2FC_cd14) == sign(avg_log2FC_fcgr3a) ~ "Shared marker",
      sig_cd14 & sig_fcgr3a ~ "Discordant",
      sig_cd14 ~ "CD14+ Mono-specific",
      sig_fcgr3a ~ "FCGR3A+ Mono-specific",
      TRUE ~ "Not significant"
    ),
    neglog10p = -log10(pmax(p_val_adj_cd14, p_val_adj_fcgr3a))
  )

# View data
head(fc_fc)
```

**Note:** For your own data the input is simply two differential analysis tables (for example DESeq2, limma or edgeR results), each containing at least a feature name and a log2 fold change column; join them by feature name before plotting.

## Visualization

### 1. Basic Plot

The basic version draws every gene as a point, with dashed threshold lines for the fold change cutoff and a dotted diagonal for reference. Points on the diagonal change equally in both contrasts.

```{r}
#| label: fig-1.1BasicFcFc
#| fig-cap: "Basic FC-FC Scatter Plot"
#| out.width: "95%"
#| warning: false
#| message: false
#| fig-width: 7.5
#| fig-height: 6

ggplot(fc_fc, aes(avg_log2FC_cd14, avg_log2FC_fcgr3a)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = c(-fc_cut, fc_cut), linetype = "dashed", color = "grey50") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = c(-fc_cut, fc_cut), linetype = "dashed", color = "grey50") +
  geom_abline(slope = 1, intercept = 0, linetype = "dotted", color = "grey60") +
  geom_point(color = "#2166AC", size = 1.8, alpha = 0.7) +
  labs(x = expression(log[2]*FC~"(CD14+ Mono vs rest)"),
       y = expression(log[2]*FC~"(FCGR3A+ Mono vs rest)")) +
  theme_bw()
```

### 2. Color by Category

Coloring genes by which contrast(s) they are significant in turns the scatter into a readable decision chart: shared markers, subset-specific markers and discordant markers each get their own color.

```{r}
#| label: fig-1.2CategoryFcFc
#| fig-cap: "Color points by significance category"
#| out.width: "95%"
#| warning: false
#| message: false
#| fig-width: 8.2
#| fig-height: 6

category_colors <- c(
  "Shared marker" = "#B2182B",
  "Discordant" = "#7B3294",
  "CD14+ Mono-specific" = "#2166AC",
  "FCGR3A+ Mono-specific" = "#1B9E77",
  "Not significant" = "grey70"
)

ggplot(fc_fc, aes(avg_log2FC_cd14, avg_log2FC_fcgr3a)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = c(-fc_cut, fc_cut), linetype = "dashed", color = "grey50") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = c(-fc_cut, fc_cut), linetype = "dashed", color = "grey50") +
  geom_point(aes(color = category), size = 2, alpha = 0.75) +
  scale_color_manual(values = category_colors) +
  labs(x = expression(log[2]*FC~"(CD14+ Mono vs rest)"),
       y = expression(log[2]*FC~"(FCGR3A+ Mono vs rest)"),
       color = "Category") +
  theme_bw()
```

::: callout-tip
**Key Parameters: **

- `fc_cut`: The fold change threshold. With `fc_cut = 0.5` a gene counts as changed when its |log2FC| ≥ 0.5 on an axis; adjust it to your data scale.
- `p_cut`: The adjusted P value cutoff used to call significance (0.05 here); it separates real markers from noise when assigning categories.
:::

### 3. Point Size and Gene Labels

Encoding statistical significance as point size and labeling the most interesting genes completes the plot: extremes on either axis, shared markers with the strongest joint evidence, and the discordant genes.

```{r}
#| label: fig-1.3LabelFcFc
#| fig-cap: "FC-FC scatter plot with significance-scaled points and curated gene labels"
#| out.width: "95%"
#| warning: false
#| message: false
#| fig-width: 9.2
#| fig-height: 6.4

# Curated label set: discordant genes, extremes on both axes and top shared markers
label_genes <- bind_rows(
  fc_fc |> filter(category == "Discordant") |>
    slice_max(abs(avg_log2FC_cd14 - avg_log2FC_fcgr3a), n = 3),
  fc_fc |> slice_max(abs(avg_log2FC_cd14), n = 3),
  fc_fc |> slice_max(abs(avg_log2FC_fcgr3a), n = 3),
  fc_fc |> filter(gene == "MS4A7"),
  fc_fc |> filter(category == "Shared marker") |>
    slice_max(neglog10p + pmin(abs(avg_log2FC_cd14), abs(avg_log2FC_fcgr3a)), n = 6)
) |>
  distinct(gene, .keep_all = TRUE)

ggplot(fc_fc, aes(avg_log2FC_cd14, avg_log2FC_fcgr3a)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = c(-fc_cut, fc_cut), linetype = "dashed", color = "grey50") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = c(-fc_cut, fc_cut), linetype = "dashed", color = "grey50") +
  geom_abline(slope = 1, intercept = 0, linetype = "dotted", color = "grey60") +
  geom_point(aes(color = category, size = neglog10p), alpha = 0.75) +
  scale_color_manual(values = category_colors) +
  scale_size_continuous(range = c(0.8, 5), name = expression(-log[10](P[adj]))) +
  geom_text_repel(data = label_genes, aes(label = gene, color = category),
                  size = 3.1, fontface = "italic", max.overlaps = 40,
                  box.padding = 0.55, segment.size = 0.25,
                  show.legend = FALSE, seed = 1) +
  labs(x = expression(log[2]*FC~"(CD14+ Mono vs rest)"),
       y = expression(log[2]*FC~"(FCGR3A+ Mono vs rest)"),
       color = "Category") +
  theme_bw()
```

Figure 3 labels the discordant genes `S100A9` and `NAP1L1`, the extreme right-hand genes `S100A8` and `LYZ` on the CD14+ axis, `MS4A7` (FCGR3A+ Mono specific), and a block of shared markers (`LST1`, `FCER1G`, `IFITM3`, `CD68`, `AIF1`, …) along the diagonal; `CCL5` and `IL32` sit in the corner where both subsets are consistently depleted. In a two-dataset comparison the same layout would highlight genes consistently changed in both cohorts versus cohort-specific hits.

## Applications

The FC-FC scatter plot is widely used when two differential contrasts should be compared feature by feature:

-   Two cell populations, tissues or conditions from the same experiment (as in the example above).
-   Discovery and validation cohorts, or two independent datasets of the same disease — consistent hits lie near the diagonal.
-   Two treatment arms tested against the same control — quadrant analysis separates shared response programs from arm-specific effects.
-   Cross-omics comparisons, e.g. transcriptome versus proteome fold changes.

To apply it to your own data, run the differential analysis of each contrast separately, join the two result tables by feature name, and reuse the code above; only the file names and column names need to change.
